topic: What happens if you fall into a black hole?
title: Into A Black Hole
idea: A black hole stretches you like spaghetti, and its size decides when: seconds inside a giant one, far outside a small one.
hook: You just fell past the edge of our galaxy's black hole.

beats.line: Not even light can get back out now.
beats.see: Behind the falling hero, a beam of light curls back and gets swallowed by the dark ring on 'light'; the stars behind him go black on 'out'.

beats.line: Your feet get pulled harder than your head, and you start to stretch.
beats.see: Feet first, the paper hero's legs lengthen on 'feet', the whole body pulls taller and thinner on 'stretch'.

beats.line: Guess how many seconds you have left.
beats.see: Big stopwatch with a blinking '?' and a guess dial; countdown starts on 'Guess'.

beats.line: Twelve point eight. Then the stretch tears you apart like spaghetti.
beats.see: Stopwatch lands on 12.8 on 'Twelve point eight'; the hero becomes a long noodle strand that spirals in on 'spaghetti'.

beats.line: Back up. Your friend, watching from far away, sees something else.
beats.see: Whoosh out on 'Back'; a friend in a paper spaceship looks through a telescope on 'friend'.

beats.line: You never quite reach the edge. You slow down, turn red and fade.
beats.see: In the telescope view the hero hangs near the ring, slows on 'slow', tints red on 'red' and dims to nothing on 'fade'.

beats.line: A small black hole rips you apart hundreds of kilometers before its edge.
beats.see: Split screen: a tiny black hole; the hero stretches and snaps far out on 'rips', a distance ruler marks 'HUNDREDS OF KM' on 'hundreds'.

beats.line: The bigger the black hole, the later the stretch.
beats.see: Small and giant black holes side by side; a stretch marker slides from far outside the small one to inside the giant one on 'later'.

end.line: Watch again and count all twelve point eight seconds.
end.see: Stopwatch resets to 0 on 'again' and starts counting as the hero falls back toward the edge (loops into hook).

description: You cross the edge of our galaxy's black hole. How many seconds until you turn into spaghetti?

facts.claim: Past the event horizon nothing, not even light, gets back out.
Tidal forces stretch a falling object (spaghettification).
At a 4.3-million-Sun black hole like Sagittarius A*, destruction by spaghettification follows 12.8 seconds after crossing the horizon.
To a distant observer the faller never quite gets there: slows, reddens and fades.
facts.source: NASA Goddard page (same URL) ; NASA black hole FAQ https://science.nasa.gov/apod/frequently-asked-questions-faqs-on-black-holes

facts.claim: Small stellar-mass black holes rip objects apart before the horizon, hundreds of kilometers out.

notes: Guess answer: 12.8 seconds. 'Our galaxy's black hole' = Sagittarius A*; NASA's 12.8 s is for a 4.3-million-Sun hole 'like' Sgr A* (Sgr A* is about that mass), acceptable shorthand but flag for review. 'Feet pulled harder than head' is the plain explanation of tidal stretching, not a separate claim. 'Kilometers' kept from FACTS rather than converting to miles. Line 2 says 'you start to stretch' right after the horizon, and destruction comes 12.8 s later, consistent with NASA; no claim of being 'fine' or 'frozen forever'.
